meta.title: Wisdom & Sound Judgment Assessment
meta.description: A 500-question reflection across 20 dimensions of practical wisdom — judgment, self-awareness, emotional regulation, humility, patience, and more.

levels.label: Sage-Like Wisdom
levels.desc: You consistently combine sound judgment, self-awareness, and emotional balance — weighing perspectives carefully and rarely reacting on impulse, even under pressure.

levels.label: Strong Wisdom
levels.desc: You show mature, well-reasoned judgment in most situations, with a few areas — like tolerating uncertainty or letting go of control — still developing.

levels.label: Developing Wisdom
levels.desc: You often pause to think things through, though emotion, ego, or impatience can sometimes override your better judgment.

levels.label: Emerging Wisdom
levels.desc: You show real moments of insight and self-control, but reactive habits or a need to be right often interrupt more thoughtful responses.

levels.label: Inconsistent Wisdom
levels.desc: Impulse, defensiveness, or narrow thinking frequently outweigh reflection in your responses. Small, deliberate pauses before reacting could make a big difference.

levels.label: Wisdom Foundations Needed
levels.desc: Your answers suggest reactive, short-term thinking currently drives most of your decisions. This is a good starting point for building reflective habits.

questions.text: Before buying a used car from a private seller, how likely are you to have a mechanic inspect it first?

How likely are you to ask a close friend or family member for honest feedback about a blind spot you might have?
After getting angry at someone, how likely are you to notice whether you were actually stressed about something unrelated?
When you succeed at something, how likely are you to assume it was entirely due to your own skill, ignoring luck or help you got?
How likely are you to recognize a repeated pattern in your past relationships or jobs and consider your own role in it?
When someone says you seem defensive, how likely are you to insist you're not, without considering it might be true?
How likely are you to notice when you're avoiding a task because you're afraid of failing at it, rather than because you're "too busy"?
Before giving advice, how likely are you to consider whether you're projecting your own experience or bias onto the other person's situation?
When you're in a bad mood, how likely are you to snap at people without realizing it's really about something else going on with you?
How likely are you to recognize when a strong reaction of yours says more about your own history than about the actual situation?
How likely are you to check in with yourself honestly about whether you're truly happy in a relationship or job, not just used to it?
When you make a mistake, how likely are you to focus on explaining why it wasn't really your fault?
How likely are you to notice your own biases when judging someone from a different background than you?
Do you assume that your first gut reaction to a person or situation is basically always accurate?
How likely are you to reflect on whether your habit of interrupting people comes from excitement, impatience, or anxiety?
After receiving praise, how likely are you to think honestly about whether you actually deserve the credit, or others helped too?
When you feel insecure about something, how likely are you to cover it up by acting overly confident rather than acknowledging the insecurity to yourself?
How likely are you to notice when your own mood is coloring how you're interpreting someone else's neutral comment?
How likely are you to ask yourself whether a goal you're chasing is really your own, or something you picked up from family or social expectations?
When someone cuts you off in traffic, how likely are you to take a breath and let it go rather than react?
During a heated argument, how likely are you to raise your voice to make your point?
When you receive a harsh email from your boss, how likely are you to wait until you've calmed down before replying?
When a family member criticizes you at a gathering, how likely are you to say something cutting back in the moment?
Before responding to an insulting comment online, how likely are you to pause and consider whether it's worth engaging?
When you're stressed about a deadline, how likely are you to take it out on people around you?
When a friend cancels plans last minute, how likely are you to respond calmly even if you're disappointed?
When your partner brings up something sensitive during an argument, how likely are you to bring up unrelated past grievances to win?
When you're stuck in a long delay (flight, appointment), how likely are you to stay composed rather than complain loudly at staff?
When someone interrupts you repeatedly in a meeting, how likely are you to snap at them in front of everyone?
When you feel your heart racing during a tense conversation, how likely are you to notice it and consciously slow yourself down?
When you lose a game or competition, how likely are you to blame the referee, the rules, or other players in the heat of the moment?
When a coworker takes credit for your idea, how likely are you to address it calmly and directly rather than fume silently or explode?
When you're hungry and tired, how likely are you to recognize it and hold off on discussing anything sensitive until you've eaten or rested?
When you make a mistake in front of others, how likely are you to stay steady instead of spiraling into panic or shame?
When someone gives you unsolicited criticism in public, how likely are you to embarrass them back immediately?
When a plan falls apart at the last minute, how likely are you to focus on next steps rather than panic?
When you're cut off mid-sentence, how likely are you to let it go and calmly return to your point rather than talk over the person?
Before sending an angry text message, how likely are you to wait and reread it later with a clearer head?
When stuck in traffic and running late, how likely are you to honk repeatedly and tailgate other cars?
When a customer or stranger is rude to you, how likely are you to stay polite rather than match their tone?
When you feel embarrassed in front of others, how likely are you to shrug it off internally rather than lash out at whoever caused it?
When you're overwhelmed at work, how likely are you to step away for a few minutes to reset instead of pushing through irritably?
When a disagreement with a friend gets tense, how likely are you to bring it up again days later still worked up, instead of having let it settle?
When someone provokes you intentionally, how likely are you to recognize what they're doing and choose not to take the bait?
When someone presents solid evidence against something you believed, how likely are you to update your opinion?
When you're proven wrong in an argument, how likely are you to keep arguing rather than admit it?
How likely are you to say "I don't know" when someone asks you something outside your expertise, rather than guessing confidently?
When you read news that confirms what you already believe, how likely are you to check the source as carefully as you would with something you disagreed with?

When an expert disagrees with your personal opinion on their subject, how likely are you to assume you probably know better anyway?
After making a confident prediction that turns out wrong, how likely are you to publicly acknowledge you were mistaken?

How likely are you to ask a genuine question in a meeting rather than pretend you already understand something?
When someone with less experience than you suggests an idea, how likely are you to dismiss it without really considering it?
How likely are you to change your position on something after hearing a genuinely compelling counterargument?

How likely are you to seek out opinions that challenge your own before making an important decision?
When you catch yourself assuming you know someone's motive, how likely are you to remind yourself that it's just a guess and could be wrong?
How likely are you to admit to your kids, team, or family that you don't have all the answers on a hard topic?
When someone corrects a small factual error you made, how likely are you to get defensive rather than just say "thanks, good catch"?
How likely are you to reconsider a strong first impression of someone after getting to know them better?
When you read only a headline, how likely are you to form and share a firm opinion without reading the full article?
How likely are you to genuinely thank someone for pointing out a flaw in your thinking, even if it stings?
When your beliefs are challenged, how likely are you to interpret it as a personal attack rather than a chance to learn?

How likely are you to say "that's a good point, I hadn't considered that" during a disagreement, when it's true?

How likely are you to consider that a strong emotional reaction to an idea might be clouding your judgment of whether it's actually true?
During an argument with your partner about chores, how likely are you to pause and consider what kind of day they've had before responding?

A friend cancels plans on you last minute. How likely are you to consider that they might be dealing with something difficult rather than assuming they don't care?

A friend gives you feedback that stings but seems accurate. How likely are you to sit with it and consider it seriously instead of getting defensive?
How likely are you to search online mainly to find a source backing up what you already said, rather than to genuinely check if it's true?
You're discussing a controversial topic with someone who disagrees with you. How likely are you to ask genuine questions to understand their reasoning rather than just waiting for your turn to talk?
How likely are you to refuse to update your opinion on a topic even after being shown solid evidence against it?

Your team's current approach isn't working, and a junior member proposes a very different plan. How likely are you to seriously weigh it on its merits rather than sticking with your original idea out of pride?
Someone is making a point you disagree with. How likely are you to let them finish and make sure you understand it before responding?
You realize you've been misremembering a fact you've stated confidently many times. How likely are you to correct yourself going forward instead of continuing to state it as before?
How likely are you to win an argument using a clever rhetorical trick even though you suspect your actual position may be weaker?
A close friend holds a strong opinion you find frustrating. How likely are you to try to genuinely understand their reasoning instead of writing them off?
How likely are you to dismiss an expert's conclusion mainly because it conflicts with your gut feeling on the topic?
You're proven wrong in front of others during a meeting. How likely are you to accept it gracefully rather than getting defensive or embarrassed?
How likely are you to keep repeating a claim you privately suspect might not be fully accurate because it makes a better story?
You encounter a well-reasoned argument for a view opposite your own on a hot-button issue. How likely are you to engage with its actual substance instead of looking for reasons to dismiss it?
You come across a claim that happens to support your side of an argument. How likely are you to fact-check it even though part of you suspects it might be shaky?
A mentor challenges an assumption you've built a lot of your thinking on. How likely are you to genuinely re-examine that assumption instead of brushing off the challenge?
How likely are you to frame a discussion as a battle to 'win' rather than as a chance to figure out what's actually true?
After a long debate, you realize both you and the other person were partly right. How likely are you to say so openly instead of quietly declaring victory?
